reason: The companion of pre-code-scroll-end-padding. The breaks that break-word, which 2.1.1 lets pre > code and pre > samp inherit, adds do not count toward min-content, so with min-width: min-content code that wraps (an author white-space: pre-wrap) would widen to its longest word, and every line would wrap past the pre's edge. femto sets overflow-wrap: anywhere, which breaks lines at the same places but counts those breaks, so code that wraps keeps the pre's width. It replaces any inherited value, not only break-word: an overflow-wrap set on the pre or an ancestor no longer reaches pre > code or pre > samp. That matters only when the code wraps, and setting overflow-wrap on the code itself restores it. With white-space: pre-wrap, a word wider than the block inside a shrink-to-fit box such as a table cell now breaks inside it instead of widening the box, as it already did in normal flow.
